GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs exhibits genuine fundamental improvement: Q1 2026 revenue of $17.23B (+14.4% YoY), EPS of $17.55 (+24.3% YoY), and management-reported annualized ROE of 19.8% (vs. trailing 14.7% in the ratios pack). The franchise is strong — #1 global M&A advisor with 32% market share, record equities revenue of $5.3B, and AWM scaling to $3.7T AUS. The consumer banking exit is complete, removing a major capital drag. However, the stock has already re-rated aggressively: P/B expanded from 1.48x to 2.32x over 12 months, and the ratios-pack P/E of 15.78x may understate true trailing valuation (FY2025 EPS of $51.32 implies ~18x). The equity risk premium over 10-year Treasuries is thin at ~189bp. GBM's ~71% revenue share leaves earnings highly cyclical. Balance-sheet leverage has increased to ~15.8x. The Basel III tailwind (2.4% capital requirement reduction) and ongoing M&A recovery (Q1 global M&A +42% YoY) provide modest near-term support, but the market has largely priced these in. Net: improving fundamentals with a franchise worth owning, but valuation has captured most of the upside, leaving a mildly positive but not compelling entry point.
